fixes.explanation: That one is true, friend, and the text says it plainly. Moses named his other son Eliezer, for Moses had said, “The God of my father was my helper and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.” (Exodus 18:4) The verse itself hands us the reason for the name. Eliezer is a name that carries a whole rescue story.

No gold and no silver here, friend. Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. (Exodus 18:12) After that, Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with him in the presence of God. Jethro was a priest of Midian (Exodus 18:1), and I think that was quite a table to sit down at.

Baked just right, and that's Moses' own answer! He replies, “Because the people come to me to inquire of God…” (Exodus 18:15) Then he adds that whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to him to judge. (Exodus 18:16) So that's the whole reason he's sitting there from morning till evening. Think about that. One man, one seat, and a line that doesn't quit. I've had days at the bakery where I felt busy, but that's a different level of busy.

problems.problem: The birth-certificate joke puts the baker in a modern parenting scenario, which the audience rules exclude.
The jewelry-box joke makes the offering and sacrifices to God the subject of the punchline. Holy things are not to be the joke.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the passage and question, without Papa Dorin’s personality or humor.
